# pulse_stream (Resource)

A user stream: a JetStream stream next to the managed `EVENTS` stream, for events that need their own retention. Its subjects must not overlap `evt.>` or Pulse's internal subjects. Deleting it deletes all its messages. Import with the stream name.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Metrics from the home lab, kept for 30 days and at most 1 GiB.
resource "pulse_stream" "metrics" {
  name            = "METRICS"
  description     = "Home lab metrics, short retention"
  subjects        = ["metrics.>"]
  max_bytes       = 1073741824
  max_age_seconds = 2592000
  compression     = true
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Stream name (letters, digits, `_` and `-`, at most 64). Changing it forces a new resource.
- `subjects` (Set of String) Subjects the stream stores (wildcards allowed).

### Optional

- `allow_direct` (Boolean) Allow direct get (fast reads by sequence or subject). Default `false`.
- `compression` (Boolean) S2 compression on disk. Default `false`.
- `description` (String) Description.
- `discard` (String) What happens when a limit is reached: `old` (default) drops the oldest messages, `new` refuses new ones.
- `duplicates_seconds` (Number) De-duplication window for `Nats-Msg-Id` in seconds (at most 86400). Defaults to the NATS default (120).
- `max_age_seconds` (Number) Maximum message age in seconds; `0` (the default) keeps messages until another limit applies.
- `max_bytes` (Number) Size limit in bytes. `-1` (the default) means unlimited.
- `max_msg_size` (Number) Largest message in bytes (at most 1048576). `-1` (the default) means unlimited.
- `max_msgs` (Number) Message count limit. `-1` (the default) means unlimited.
- `storage` (String) `file` (default) or `memory`. Changing it forces a new resource.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import pulse_stream.metrics METRICS
```
